_why: THE SHARE IS AHEAD OF THE REPO ON CONTENT, AND BEHIND IT ON MEASUREMENTS (#1313).
site_b/MANIFEST.json is the site_a story a second time. Field values were applied
to the per-site file BY HAND and never reached the committed profile, so an
ordinary `populate_archive.py` run would have copied studio-b.assets.json over the
top and stripped all 1,306 records of 6,806 values. Measured 2026-08-27 against the
live share; `manifest_guard.py` reproduces it, and refuses it.
This document carries that advantage back so the repair is reproducible from the
REPO ALONE. The share is not a dependency of the pipeline: a test that needed it
would pass on a workstation and fail on a runner, which is the same shape as the
bug it is fixing.
fill   6,806 field_values entries across all 1,306 records, in eleven keys:
production_area (1,306), country (1,306), keywords (1,306), credit (653),
production_notes (436), copyright (436), usage_rights (327),
capture_date (327), ingested_at (262), license_expires (262),
derived_from (185).
added  NOTHING. Unlike site_a there is no orphan: the two sides hold the same
1,306 ids, in both directions.
THE PASS THAT APPLIES THIS CAN ONLY ADD, NEVER REPLACE (see
`apply_upgrade.apply_manifest_reconcile`). That is what makes it idempotent and
what stops it undoing a later edit.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, AND WHY THE DIRECTION WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED. 392 `file_size_bytes` differ with both sides non-empty, and on all 392 the
share's number matches the bytes lying at the share. That looks decisive and is
not: it proves only that the share is self-consistent. All 392 are `hq` records,
which are COPIED FROM the kenney-hq pool, so the question is which side agrees with
the pool. Built fresh on 2026-08-27 from the committed kenney-hq-pool.json (945
vectors rendered, 86 bitmaps copied), the pool matches the PROFILE on all 656 of
site_b's hq records and the share on only 264. The share holds an older pool build.
Writing its numbers in would have corrupted 392 correct records and made the very
next build refuse its own input.
So the remedy for those 392 is to REPUBLISH site_b, not to edit the profile.
`manifest_guard.py` classifies them CHANGED_VALUE, which is a report rather than
a refusal, so they never block a publish.
42 `title` and 6 `metadata.sha256` values also differ with both sides non-empty.
Titles are CONTENT and the profile owns them outright (the seeded titles were
rewritten in #1306). The six hashes are 2 `hq` and 4 `internet`: the hq pair is
source-backed like the byte counts above, and an `internet` record's hash is its
IDENTITY rather than a measurement, because the asset id derives from it.
DO NOT hand-edit site_b/MANIFEST.json again. It is an OUTPUT. That habit is what
created this document, twice.
